newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Banque Indosuez to expand business in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Banque Indosuez to expand business in Bangladesh.

text.p: French Banque Indosuez has doubled its capital of its Bangladesh operation to 400 million taka ($9.3 million), a financial daily said on Monday.

"The increased capital will be invested in syndicated lending with local banks, securities business and automation of its fund transfer and other systems," The Financial Express quoted Jean-Claude Gruffat, the bank's chairman for Asia and Pacific region, as saying in Dhaka on Sunday.
Gruffat, who is based in Singapore and now on a visit to Dhaka, said his bank expected significant growth in business in Bangladesh in view of the country's liberal economic policies.
"The policies that Bangladesh is now pursuing are favourable to foreign investment. We are expecting growth in our business here," the Indosuez executive said.
Gruffat said his bank considered Asia "a very important" market and its assessment of Bangladesh "is also impressive".
Indosuez has banking branches in Dhaka and Chittagong and has been in operation in Bangladesh since 1981. It finances nearly four percent of the country's total import and export trade.
Meanwhile, Hongkong Bank, a member of the UK-based Hong Kong Shanghai Banking Corporation (HSBC), started operations in Bangladesh on Sunday, local newspapers reported on Monday.
The visiting chairman of the HSBC group, John Strickland, told the launching ceremony in Dhaka on Sunday that his bank would offer security to foreign investors willing to invest in Bangladesh.
